steps.text: Discourse markers typically go at the start of a sentence or clause. They do not change the grammar — they add attitude and flow.
steps.auma: klaro, tu pude beni! · serio, mi neda akwa · aktua, mi no pude
steps.english: of course, you can come! · seriously, I need water · actually, I cannot

steps.question: How do you say 'look, the weather is very good today!'?
options: mira klima hodi esi mui bona!
klima mira esi mui bona hodi!
mira, klima esi mui bona hodi!
steps.explanation: mira at the start: mira, klima esi mui bona hodi!

steps.question: How do you say 'alright, so what do you want?'
steps.explanation: bweno and enton stack naturally: bweno, enton kosa tu voli?

lessons.title: The Mind
lessons.subtitle: Decide, believe, prove, know — verbs of thought and judgment.

steps.title: The Mind
steps.text: Foundation gave you pensa (think) and senti (feel). Now you gain verbs for the full range of mental activity — deciding, believing, proving, knowing, doubting, paying, dreaming, and standing firm.
steps.auma: mi pensa → mi deside · mi senti → mi kreda
steps.english: I think → I decide · I feel → I believe

steps.sentence: mi deside a anda en matina
steps.translation: I decide to walk in the morning

steps.sentence: mi kreda ke tu esi bona
steps.translation: I believe that you are good

steps.sentence: tu prova ke tu esi forta
steps.translation: you prove that you are strong

steps.title: Using ke (that) with mental verbs
steps.text: You learned ke in Foundation as a conjunction. With mental verbs, ke introduces what you think, believe, know, or doubt. The pattern is: subject + verb + ke + clause.
steps.auma: mi kreda ke natura esi bona · mi sabe ke tu pude koka
steps.english: I believe that nature is good · I know that you can cook

steps.question: How do you say 'I decide that I must run'?
options: deside mi ke mi debe kuri
mi deside ke mi debe kuri
steps.explanation: mi deside ke (I decide that) + mi debe kuri (I must run).

steps.sentence: mi no duba ke tu esi ami
steps.translation: I do not doubt that you are a friend

steps.title: Building complex thoughts
steps.text: With these verbs you can express belief, decision, doubt, knowledge, and dreams. Combined with modals and question words, your sentences become rich and natural.
steps.auma: mi kreda ke we pude trova armoni · keno tu duba? · mi ruma ke mi flugi supra monta
steps.english: I believe that we can find harmony · why do you doubt? · I dream that I soar above the mountain

steps.question: How do you say 'I know that the river is cold'?
options: sabe mi ke rivo esi frida
mi sabe ke rivo esi frida
steps.explanation: mi sabe ke (I know that) + rivo esi frida (the river is cold).

steps.question: How do you say 'they dream at night and stand in the morning'?
options: tali ruma e standi en noka en matina
en noka tali ruma e en matina standi
tali ruma en noka e standi en matina
steps.explanation: Two actions joined with e: tali ruma en noka e standi en matina.

lessons.title: The Checkpoint
lessons.subtitle: Week 5 review — questions, modals, comparisons, and conversation flow.

steps.title: Week 5 Checkpoint
steps.text: You have unlocked conversational mastery tools: question words (sapa, kosa, ketu, kemo, keno, komo, kwanto), modals (pude, debe, devri, moga, neda), comparisons (plu, maks, min, mui, tro, basta, kasi), time depth (semana, mensa, anua, tempo, hori), discourse markers (klaro, beno, enton, serio), and mental verbs (deside, kreda, sabe, duba). Now practice combining them all.

steps.title: Conversation practice
steps.text: Read this exchange aloud. Every word is from Foundation or Week 5.
steps.auma:
A: salama! komo tu senti hodi?
B: beno, mi senti tipo lasa. mi no domi bona en noka.
A: serio? keno tu no pude domi?
B: mi pensa tro. mi debe ruma plu kalma.
A: klaro. tu devri beva teo en sera. teo esi mui kalma.
B: bweno, mi deside ke mi beva teo hodi sera. gratao, ami.
A: klaro! mi sabe ke tu pude senti plu bona doma.
B: mi kreda ke tu esi bona. adio!
steps.english:
A: Hello! How do you feel today?
B: Well, I feel sort of tired. I did not sleep well at night.
A: Seriously? Why could you not sleep?
B: I think too much. I must dream more calmly.
A: Of course. You should drink tea in the evening. Tea is very calming.
B: Alright, I decide that I will drink tea this evening. Thank you, friend.
A: Of course! I know that you can feel better tomorrow.
B: I believe that you are right. Goodbye!

steps.question: How do you ask 'who can sing the most?'
steps.explanation: sapa (who) + pude kanta (can sing) + maks bona (the best).

steps.question: How do you say 'I know that we must pay at the market'?
options: mi sabe we debe lipa en merkato
sabe mi ke we lipa debe en merkato
mi sabe ke we debe lipa en merkato
steps.explanation: mi sabe ke (I know that) + we debe lipa (we must pay) + en merkato (at the market).

steps.question: How do you say 'actually, the year has four seasons'?
steps.explanation: aktua at the start: aktua, anua teni fo sezoni.

steps.question: Build this sentence: 'I almost decided, but I doubt'
options: mi deside kasi, pero mi duba
kasi mi deside, pero duba mi
mi kasi deside, pero mi duba
steps.explanation: mi kasi deside (I almost decided) + pero (but) + mi duba (I doubt).

lessons.title: The Abstract
lessons.subtitle: Idea, purpose, destiny, meaning — the vocabulary of thought.

steps.title: The Abstract
steps.text: Foundation gave you spirito, natura, libra, verao. Now you go deeper into the vocabulary of thought — idea, purpose, destiny, force, meaning, consciousness, thought, and memory. In v12, kira is consciousness/living knowledge; konosia is factual or stored knowledge; sabe is the verb to know.
steps.auma: mi pensa → mi teni idea · mi sabe → mi teni konosia · mi senti kira
steps.english: I think → I have an idea · I know → I have knowledge · I feel consciousness

steps.question: How do you say 'my purpose is to find truth'?
options: purpusa di mi esi trova verao
trova verao esi purpusa di mi
steps.explanation: purpusa di mi (my purpose) + esi (is) + trova verao (to find truth).

steps.sentence: kosa esi signifa di iti vorto?
steps.translation: what is the meaning of this word?

steps.sentence: penso di mi esi klaro hodi

steps.title: Abstract nouns in sentences
steps.text: Abstract nouns work exactly like concrete nouns. They follow the same subject + verb + object pattern and can be possessed with di.
steps.auma: idea di tu esi mui bona · mi sabe ke kira esi en mi · signifa di ama esi granda
steps.english: your idea is very good · I know that consciousness is in me · the meaning of love is great

steps.question: How do you ask 'what is the meaning of this?'
steps.explanation: kosa esi (what is) + signifa di iti (the meaning of this).

steps.question: How do you say 'memory is stronger than thought'?
options: penso esi min forta ke memo
memo esi plu forta ke penso
steps.explanation: memo esi plu forta ke penso (memory is stronger than thought).

lessons.title: The Bond
lessons.subtitle: Joke, laugh, hug, kiss — the social gestures that connect us.

steps.title: The Bond
steps.text: Foundation taught you festa, dansa, musika, kanta for celebration. Now you learn the intimate social words — joking, laughing, hugging, kissing, promising, secrets, trust, and face/dignity.
steps.auma: we dansa → we joka e riso
steps.english: we dance → we joke and laugh

steps.sentence: mi joka kon ami di mi

steps.translation: I give a hug to my mother

steps.question: How do you say 'we laugh and hug at the festival'?
options: we riso abraso en festa e
riso we e abraso en festa dona
we riso e dona abraso en festa
steps.explanation: we riso e dona abraso en festa.

steps.translation: I give a promise to you

steps.sentence: mianzi esi mui importa en komunita
steps.translation: face is very important in community

steps.title: Social bonds in Auma
steps.text: These words describe the gestures and trust that hold communities together. Notice how they combine naturally with Foundation words like dona (give), ami (friend), and komunita (community).
steps.auma: mi konfida en ami di mi · we dona promisa a komunita di we · mi teni sekreta pero mi devri parla
steps.english: I trust in my friend · we give a promise to our community · I have a secret but I should speak

steps.question: How do you say 'I promise that I will not reveal the secret'?
options: dona mi promisa ke sekreta mi no parla
mi dona promisa ke mi no parla sekreta
mi promisa no parla sekreta dona
steps.explanation: mi dona promisa ke (I promise that) + mi no parla sekreta (I will not speak the secret).

steps.question: How do you ask 'who do you trust?'
steps.explanation: sapa (who) + tu konfida en (do you trust in).

lessons.title: The Digital
lessons.subtitle: Computer, phone, network, screen — technology in Auma.

steps.title: The Digital
steps.text: The modern world needs modern words. Auma has a full technology vocabulary that follows the same transparent patterns. No irregular forms — just new nouns and verbs for the digital world.

steps.translation: the network is in the house

steps.question: How do you say 'I read a book on the computer'?
steps.explanation: mi legi libro (I read a book) + en komputa (on the computer).

steps.translation: I send a message to a friend
the message from a friend is good
I receive a message from a friend

steps.title: Digital communication
steps.text: senda (send) and resiva (receive) pair naturally with mesaja (message), letera (letter), and the prepositions a (to) and de (from).
steps.auma: mi senda mesaja a amili di mi · mi resiva letera de mama · mi tekla en telefona
steps.english: I send a message to my family · I receive a letter from my mother · I type on the phone

steps.question: How do you ask 'when do you send the message?'
steps.explanation: kemo (when, question) + tu senda mesaja (do you send the message).

steps.question: How do you say 'the phone screen is too small'?
options: skirmo di telefona esi tro pika
skirmo telefona di esi pika tro
steps.explanation: skirmo di telefona (the phone screen) + esi tro pika (is too small).

lessons.title: The Exchange
lessons.subtitle: Price, reserve, contract, cancel — the language of business.

steps.title: The Exchange
steps.text: Business and commerce use the same sentence patterns as everything else in Auma. Learn eight essential words for prices, contracts, and transactions.

steps.translation: I reserve a building in the city

steps.question: How do you ask 'what is the price of coffee?'
steps.explanation: kosa esi preka di kopi?

steps.sentence: mi anda a ofisa en matina
steps.translation: I go to the office in the morning
I have an account on the internet

steps.title: Business conversation
steps.text: Combine these with modals and question words for natural business exchanges at the merkato or ofisa.
steps.auma: mi voli rezerva, plisa · kosa esi preka? · mi pude kansela? · mi debe lipa nau
steps.english: I want to reserve, please · what is the price? · can I cancel? · I must pay now

steps.question: How do you say 'I must cancel the reservation'?
steps.explanation: mi debe (I must) + kansela (cancel) + rezerva (reservation).

steps.question: How do you say 'the office is in the city'?
steps.explanation: ofisa esi en sita (the office is in the city).

steps.translation: they sell fruit at the market

lessons.title: The Season
lessons.subtitle: Summer, winter, spring, autumn — the rhythm of the year.

steps.title: The Season
steps.text: You learned sezoni (season) on Day 32. Now you name the seasons themselves — summer, winter, spring, autumn, dry season, and rainy season. Plus two time-quality words.

steps.translation: the tree is golden in autumn

steps.question: How do you ask 'which season do you like most?'
steps.explanation: kosa sezoni (which season) + tu ama maks (do you love most).

steps.translation: dry season is hot and dry

steps.title: Seasons in conversation
steps.text: Seasons are nouns that work like any other. Use them with prepositions, comparisons, and question words.
steps.auma: mi ama verino plu ke hiverno · estino esi maks varma · en otunio mi senti kalma · pluvino dona akwa
steps.english: I love spring more than winter · summer is the hottest · in autumn I feel calm · rainy season gives water

steps.question: How do you say 'winter is colder than autumn'?
options: otunio esi min frida ke hiverno
hiverno esi plu frida ke otunio
steps.explanation: hiverno esi plu frida ke otunio (winter is colder than autumn).

steps.question: How do you say 'time moves slowly in winter'?
options: tempo esi lenta mota en hiverno
steps.explanation: tempo mota lenta (time moves slowly) + en hiverno (in winter).

lessons.title: The Depth
lessons.subtitle: Inspired, creative, focused, cozy — the nuanced emotions.

steps.title: The Depth
steps.text: Foundation gave you basic emotions — hapi, trisa, ira, kalma. Now you explore the nuanced emotional landscape: inspired, courageous-hearted, creative, cozy, focused, distracted, tense, and patient.

steps.sentence: mi senti inspira kwando mi legi
steps.translation: I feel inspired when I read
the house is cozy in winter

steps.question: How do you say 'I feel inspired and creative'?
steps.explanation: mi senti inspira e kreati.

steps.sentence: mi esi foka kwando mi skrivi
steps.translation: I am focused when I write
I am distracted in the office

steps.title: Emotional nuance
steps.text: These words let you describe subtle inner states. Combine them with modals, comparisons, and discourse markers for authentic expression.
steps.auma: mi senti plu inspira en matina · mi esi tro tensa, mi neda esi plu kalma · aktua, mi senti huga en tomo
steps.english: I feel more inspired in the morning · I am too tense, I need to be calmer · actually, I feel cozy at home

steps.question: How do you say 'you should be more focused and less distracted'?
options: tu devri plu foka e min distra esi
tu devri esi plu foka e min distra
plu foka tu devri esi e min distra
steps.explanation: tu devri esi (you should be) + plu foka e min distra (more focused and less distracted).

steps.question: How do you say 'patience is very important'?
steps.explanation: sabar esi mui importa (patience is very important).

steps.translation: I feel trauma in the heart.

steps.sentence: si tu senti reakta, atenda e beva akwa
steps.translation: If you feel activated, wait and drink water.
I feel avoidance in the heart.
I feel defensive in the heart.
I feel denial in the heart.

lessons.title: The Checkpoint
lessons.subtitle: Week 6 review — culture, technology, business, and emotional depth.

steps.title: Week 6 Checkpoint
steps.text: This week you explored culture and expression: abstract concepts (idea, purpusa, destina, signifa, kira, penso, memo), social bonds (joka, riso, abraso, besa, promisa, sekreta, konfida), technology (komputa, telefona, reta, skirmo, tekla, klika, senda, resiva), business (preka, rezerva, kontrato, diskonto, kansela, ofisa, konto, karga), seasons (verino, estino, otunio, hiverno, sekino, pluvino), and nuanced emotions (inspira, kori, kreati, huga, foka, distra, tensa, sabar).

steps.title: Extended reading
steps.text: Read this passage aloud. It combines Foundation and Expansion vocabulary.
steps.auma: salama, ami! komo tu senti hodi? mi esi inspira porke verino esi inspira. mi senda mesaja a amili di mi en telefona. mi skrivi: salama! mira, flora kresa en parko! mi teni idea nova — we devri dona festa en komunita di we kwando estino beni. we pude koka sopa e kani fruta. mi debe lipa preka en merkato pero mi kreda ke diskonto esi bona. mi konfida en tu. tu esi kori e kreati. enton, kosa tu pensa? mi senti huga kwando we esi en tomo kon amili di we. adio!
steps.english: Hello, friend! How do you feel today? I am inspired because spring is near. I send a message to my family on the phone. I write: Hello! Look, flowers grow in the park! I have a new idea — we should have a festival in our community when summer comes. We can cook soup and eat fruit. I must pay the price at the market but I believe that the discount is good. I trust in you. You are courageous and creative. So, what do you think? I feel cozy when we are at home with our family. Goodbye!

steps.question: How do you say 'I send a promise to my community'?
options: mi dona promisa senda a komunita
mi senda promisa a komunita di mi
senda mi promisa a komunita di mi
steps.explanation: mi senda promisa (I send a promise) + a komunita di mi (to my community).

steps.question: How do you say 'consciousness is the force of thought'?
steps.explanation: kira esi (consciousness is) + forsa di penso (the force of thought).

steps.question: How do you ask 'can I cancel the reservation?'
steps.explanation: ka + mi pude kansela rezerva: ka mi pude kansela rezerva?

steps.question: How do you say 'I joke and laugh when I am with friends'?
options: mi joka e riso kwando mi esi kon amili
kwando mi esi kon amili mi joka riso e
mi joka riso kwando mi esi amili kon
steps.explanation: mi joka e riso (I joke and laugh) + kwando mi esi kon amili (when I am with friends).

lessons.title: The Healing
lessons.subtitle: Medicine, health, balance, rest — body and wellness vocabulary.

steps.title: The Healing
steps.text: Foundation taught you korpo (body), kora (heart), dolo (pain), sana (heal). Now you expand into the full health vocabulary — medicine, wellness, balance, rest, energy, strength, cure, and life.

steps.sentence: tu debe reposa kwando tu esi lasa
steps.translation: you must rest when you are tired

steps.question: How do you say 'health is more important than money'?
steps.explanation: sanita esi plu importa (health is more important).

steps.sentence: mi teni molta eneria en matina
steps.translation: I have much energy in the morning

steps.title: Health philosophy in Auma
steps.text: Auma health vocabulary connects body, mind, and spirit. Balance, rest, energy, and strength are all part of the same conversation.
steps.auma: mi neda balansa inter eneria e reposa · kurita beni de natura e kalma · fortia di korpo e fortia di penso esi mui importa
steps.english: I need balance between energy and rest · healing comes from nature and calm · strength of body and strength of mind are very important

steps.question: How do you say 'I need to rest because I have no energy'?
options: porke mi no teni eneria mi neda reposa
mi reposa neda porke mi eneria no teni
mi neda reposa porke mi no teni eneria
steps.explanation: mi neda reposa (I need to rest) + porke (because) + mi no teni eneria (I have no energy).

steps.question: How do you say 'life has balance between strength and rest'?
options: vita teni balansa inter fortia e reposa
vita esi balansa fortia e reposa inter
balansa di vita teni fortia e reposa
steps.explanation: vita teni balansa (life has balance) + inter fortia e reposa (between strength and rest).

lessons.title: The Wild
lessons.subtitle: Coral, island, forest, butterfly — the deeper natural world.

steps.title: The Wild
steps.text: Foundation gave you monta, mara, arbo, flora. Now you explore the wilder side of nature — coral reefs, islands, forests, butterflies, palm trees, lotus flowers, bamboo, and coconut.

steps.translation: the island is in the blue sea
the forest is green and big
the butterfly flies in the forest

steps.question: How do you say 'the island has a beautiful forest'?
steps.explanation: isla teni boski bona (the island has a beautiful forest).

steps.translation: palm trees grow on the island
the lotus is the flower of calm

steps.title: Describing the wild world
steps.text: These nature words combine beautifully with comparisons, prepositions, and your full vocabulary for rich descriptions of the natural world.
steps.auma: korali esi plu bona ke petra en mara · maripi esi maks bona en boski · mi senti inspira kwando mi esi en isla
steps.english: coral is more beautiful than rock in the sea · the butterfly is the most beautiful in the forest · I feel inspired when I am on the island

steps.question: How do you say 'bamboo is the fastest-growing plant'?
steps.explanation: bambu kresa maks rapida (bamboo grows the fastest).

steps.question: How do you say 'I find lotus flowers at the river'?
steps.explanation: mi trova loto (I find lotus) + en rivo (at the river).

lessons.title: The Position
lessons.subtitle: Against, far, around, through — advanced spatial relationships.

steps.title: The Position
steps.text: Foundation gave you en, a, sub, supra, inter, kon. Now you add advanced prepositions that express opposition, distance, surrounding, passing through, nearness, absence, purpose, and movement under.

steps.sentence: isla esi lonta de tomo di mi
steps.translation: the island is far from my house
the river moves through the forest

steps.question: How do you say 'the bird flies through the forest'?
steps.explanation: avi flugi (the bird flies) + tra boski (through the forest).

steps.translation: the cafe is near the park

steps.sentence: mi no pude domi sen kalma
mi koka por amili di mi

steps.translation: the fish swims under the wave

steps.title: Prepositions in rich sentences
steps.text: Stack prepositions with your full vocabulary to describe complex spatial relationships and purposes.
steps.auma: mi anda tra boski e sirka parko por trova kalma · tomo di mi esi proksima mara pero lonta de merkato · we standi kontra pluva sen dolo
steps.english: I walk through the forest and around the park to find calm · my house is near the sea but far from the market · we stand against the rain without pain

steps.question: How do you say 'I cook for my friend without bread'?
options: mi koka sen pano por ami di mi
por ami di mi mi koka sen pano
mi koka por ami di mi sen pano
steps.explanation: mi koka (I cook) + por ami di mi (for my friend) + sen pano (without bread).

steps.question: How do you say 'the temple is near the mountain'?
steps.explanation: templo esi proksima monta (the temple is near the mountain).

lessons.title: The Feast
lessons.subtitle: Food, honey, flavor, spice — the richer vocabulary of eating.

steps.title: The Feast
steps.text: Foundation gave you akwa, pano, kopi, teo, sopa, fruta, karni, ovo. Now you deepen the food vocabulary with words for food itself, honey, flavor, spice, sugar, salt, cheese, and hunger.

steps.sentence: manja esi mui importa por vita
steps.translation: food is very important for life

steps.sentence: sabora di sopa esi mui bona
steps.translation: the flavor of the soup is very good

steps.question: How do you say 'the honey has a good flavor'?
steps.explanation: miela teni sabora bona (the honey has a good flavor).

steps.title: Describing food and meals
steps.text: Combine food words with flavors, comparisons, and feelings for rich descriptions of meals and eating.
steps.auma: mi senti hambre en sera · sabora di keso esi plu forta ke sabora di pano · mi koka kon salo, spisao, e miela
steps.english: I feel hungry in the evening · the flavor of cheese is stronger than the flavor of bread · I cook with salt, spice, and honey

steps.question: How do you say 'I am too hungry, I need food'?
options: tro hambre mi esi, neda mi manja
mi esi tro hambre, mi neda manja
mi tro hambre esi, mi manja neda
steps.explanation: mi esi tro hambre (I am too hungry) + mi neda manja (I need food).

steps.question: How do you ask 'does the soup need more salt?'
steps.explanation: ka + sopa neda plu salo: ka sopa neda plu salo?

lessons.title: The Absence
lessons.subtitle: Nothing, nowhere, no one, no way — the complete negation system.

steps.title: The Absence
steps.text: Foundation gave you no (not). Auma has a complete negation system built from question words: nokemo (never), nokeno (for no reason), nomodo (in no way), nosapa (no one). Plus words for emptiness and falseness.
steps.auma: no → nokemo, nokeno, nomodo, nosapa
steps.english: not → never, for no reason, in no way, no one

steps.sentence: mi nokemo senti sola en komunita
steps.translation: I never feel alone in community
I am not angry for no reason
this is in no way good

steps.title: The negation pattern
steps.text: Each negation word mirrors a question word: kemo (when?) becomes nokemo (never), keno (why?) becomes nokeno (for no reason), komo (how?) becomes nomodo (in no way), sapa (who?) becomes nosapa (no one). This is systematic — no memorization needed.
steps.auma: kemo → nokemo · keno → nokeno · komo → nomodo · sapa → nosapa
steps.english: when? → never · why? → for no reason · how? → in no way · who? → no one

steps.question: How do you say 'no one can fly'?
steps.explanation: nosapa pude flugi (no one can fly). nosapa already contains the negation.

steps.sentence: malu no esi forta ke bona
steps.translation: bad is not stronger than good

steps.title: Negation in conversation
steps.text: These words let you express absence, emptiness, and falseness with precision. They make your Auma more nuanced and natural.
steps.auma: mi nokemo parla falsa vorto · nosapa pude esi en du tomo en un tempo · tomo vakua dona kalma
steps.english: I never speak false words · no one can be in two places at the same time · an empty room gives calm

steps.question: How do you say 'I never eat without salt'?
options: mi no kani nokemo sen salo
steps.explanation: mi nokemo kani sen salo (I never eat without salt).

steps.question: How do you say 'the house is empty, there is nothing'?
options: tomo esi vakua, nulao esi en ita
tomo esi vakua, esi nulao en ita
steps.explanation: tomo esi vakua (the house is empty) + nulao esi en ita (nothing is in it).

lessons.title: The Voice
lessons.subtitle: Opinion, poem, sign, art — deeper communication words.

steps.title: The Voice
steps.text: Foundation gave you vorto, frasa, lingwa, libro, mesaja. Now you deepen into opinion, poetry, signs, art, story, fact, song (noun), and the English language word.

steps.sentence: mi skrivi poema por ami di mi
steps.translation: I write a poem for my friend
the sign is on the road
art is the language of the heart

steps.question: How do you say 'I believe that art is very important'?
options: mi kreda ke arto esi mui importa
mi kreda ke mui importa esi arto
mi kreda arto esi mui importa
steps.explanation: mi kreda ke (I believe that) + arto esi mui importa (art is very important).

steps.translation: the elder speaks the story of the community
this is a fact, not an opinion

steps.title: Communication and culture
steps.text: With these words you can discuss opinion versus fact, appreciate art and poetry, tell stories, and talk about languages.
steps.auma: opina di mi esi ke poema esi maks bona via di arto · storia di tana teni konosia · fakta esi bona, opina pude esi falsa
steps.english: my opinion is that poetry is the most beautiful form of art · the elder's story has wisdom · facts are good, opinions can be false

steps.question: How do you say 'I write songs and poems in Auma'?
options: mi skrivi en auma kanto e poema
en auma mi skrivi kanto poema e
mi skrivi kanto e poema en auma
steps.explanation: mi skrivi kanto e poema en auma.

steps.question: How do you ask 'do you speak English or Auma?'
options: ka tu parla angla o auma?
ka parla tu angla o auma?
tu parla angla o auma ka?
steps.explanation: ka tu parla angla o auma?

lessons.title: The Checkpoint
lessons.subtitle: Week 7 review — health, nature, food, negation, and voice.

steps.title: Week 7 Checkpoint
steps.text: This week took you deeper: health and healing (medika, sanita, balansa, reposa, eneria, fortia, kurita, vita), wild nature (korali, isla, boski, maripi, palma, loto, bambu, koko), advanced prepositions (kontra, lonta, sirka, tra, proksima, sen, por, suba), rich food vocabulary (manja, miela, sabora, spisao, dulsa, salo, keso, hambre), the complete negation system (nokemo, nokeno, nomodo, nosapa, nulao, falsa, vakua, malu), and deeper communication (opina, poema, signo, arto, storia, fakta, kanto, angla).

steps.title: Conversation practice
steps.text: Read this dialogue aloud. It uses vocabulary from all seven weeks.
steps.auma:
A: salama! komo tu senti? mi rongo ke tu esi malu sanita.
B: ya, mi esi lasa e mi senti dolo. mi neda medika.
A: tu debe reposa e beva teo kon miela. miela dona kurita.
B: gratao. mi nokemo senti hambre kwando mi esi malu sanita.
A: mi koka sopa por tu — kon salo e spisao. sabora esi bona.
B: tu esi mui kori. mi kreda ke fortia beni de reposa e manja bona.
A: klaro. mi skrivi poema por tu: vita esi bona kwando we teni balansa.
B: iti esi bona arto. mi senti plu kalma ya. gratao, ami!
steps.english:
A: Hello! How do you feel? I hear that you are in bad health.
B: Yes, I am tired and I feel pain. I need medicine.
A: You must rest and drink tea with honey. Honey gives healing.
B: Thanks. I never feel hungry when I am in bad health.
A: I cook soup for you — with salt and spice. The flavor is good.
B: You are very brave-hearted. I believe that strength comes from rest and good food.
A: Of course. I write a poem for you: life is good when we have balance.
B: That is good art. I feel calmer already. Thank you, friend!

steps.question: How do you say 'no one can find the island without a sign'?
options: nosapa pude trova isla sen signo
sen signo nosapa pude isla trova
nosapa trova pude isla sen signo
steps.explanation: nosapa pude trova isla (no one can find the island) + sen signo (without a sign).

steps.question: How do you say 'the forest is far from the city but near the river'?
options: lonta de sita boski esi pero proksima rivo
boski esi lonta sita pero proksima rivo de
boski esi lonta de sita pero proksima rivo
steps.explanation: boski esi lonta de sita (forest is far from the city) + pero proksima rivo (but near the river).

steps.question: How do you say 'this is a fact: honey is sweet and golden'?
options: iti fakta esi: dulsa e dora miela esi
fakta iti esi: miela dulsa e dora esi
iti esi fakta: miela esi dulsa e dora
steps.explanation: iti esi fakta (this is a fact) + miela esi dulsa e dora (honey is sweet and golden).

lessons.title: The Wisdom
lessons.subtitle: Hope, goodness, beauty, knowledge — abstract philosophy.

steps.title: The Wisdom
steps.text: You have been learning Auma for fifty days. Now you learn the deepest abstract words — hope (as noun), goodness, beauty, wisdom, knowledge, dream (as noun), the word Auma itself, and ubuntu — the philosophy that 'I am because we are.'

steps.sentence: sorao esi en kora di we

steps.translation: the beauty of nature is great

steps.question: How do you say 'beauty and goodness are in all life'?
options: belina e bonina esi en tota vita
belina bonina esi en tota vita e
en tota vita belina e bonina esi
steps.explanation: belina e bonina (beauty and goodness) + esi en tota vita (are in all life).

steps.translation: Auma is the language of consciousness
ubuntu is the belief of community

steps.title: Philosophy in Auma
steps.text: These are the words that live at the intersection of language and consciousness. Auma is not just a language — it is a way of seeing. Ubuntu teaches that we exist through each other.
steps.auma: mi sabe porke auma esi lingwa di kira: en auma, tota vorto teni signifa · sabina beni de konosia · bonina e belina esi en ubuntu
steps.english: I know why Auma is the language of consciousness: in Auma, every word has meaning · wisdom comes from knowledge · goodness and beauty are in ubuntu

steps.question: How do you say 'wisdom comes from knowledge and time'?
options: sabina de konosia e tempo beni
sabina beni de konosia e tempo
konosia e tempo dona sabina beni
steps.explanation: sabina beni de (wisdom comes from) + konosia e tempo (knowledge and time).

steps.question: How do you say 'my dream is that we all feel unity'?
options: mi sonia ke we senti unita esi
sonia mi di esi ke senti we unita
sonia di mi esi ke we senti unita
steps.explanation: sonia di mi esi ke (my dream is that) + we senti unita (we all feel unity).

steps.translation: We use a ritual phrase in ritual.
We use a hand sign in ritual.

lessons.title: The Mastery
lessons.subtitle: Hide, confirm, verify, restart — advanced action verbs.

steps.title: The Mastery
steps.text: Your verb vocabulary grows with advanced actions — hide, confirm, verify, restart, celebrate, breathe, practice, and play. These follow the same patterns as all Auma verbs.

steps.sentence: mi rekina e mi senti nova
steps.translation: I restart and I feel new

steps.question: How do you say 'I must confirm and verify the contract'?
options: mi debe kontrato konfirma e verifi
mi debe konfirma e verifi kontrato
konfirma e verifi mi debe kontrato
steps.explanation: mi debe (I must) + konfirma e verifi (confirm and verify) + kontrato (the contract).

steps.translation: the child plays in the park

steps.title: Advanced actions in sentences
steps.text: These verbs combine with modals, question words, and discourse markers for sophisticated expression.
steps.auma: keno tu eskondi iti? · mi devri pratika plu · we selebra kwando we esi hapi · respira, tu pude esi kalma
steps.english: why do you hide this? · I should practice more · we celebrate when we are happy · breathe, you can be calm

steps.question: How do you say 'the child plays and celebrates in the park'?
options: sina en parko juga e selebra
sina selebra e juga en parko
sina juga e selebra en parko
steps.explanation: sina (child) + juga e selebra (plays and celebrates) + en parko (in the park).

steps.question: How do you say 'breathe deeply and restart'?
steps.explanation: respira e rekina (breathe and restart).

lessons.title: The Measure
lessons.subtitle: Meter, kilogram, liter, degree — units and measurements.

steps.title: The Measure
steps.text: Auma uses the metric system with transparent, recognizable measurement words. These are nouns that follow the same patterns as everything else.

steps.translation: the tree is ten meters tall
the market is three kilometers away

steps.sentence: mi porta du kilogramo di fruta
steps.translation: I carry two kilograms of fruit

steps.question: How do you say 'the mountain is two thousand meters tall'?
options: monta alta esi du mila metro
monta esi du mila metro alta
steps.explanation: monta esi du mila metro alta (the mountain is two thousand meters tall).

steps.sentence: mi beva du litro di akwa
steps.translation: I drink two liters of water

steps.title: Measurements in conversation
steps.text: Use measurements with numbers and di (of) for precise descriptions. The number comes before the unit.
steps.auma: kwanto kilometro tu kuri? · mi neda un litro di lakto · klima esi fo-des degreo — tro varma!
steps.english: how many kilometers do you run? · I need one liter of milk · the temperature is forty degrees — too hot!

steps.question: How do you say 'the discount is ten percent'?
steps.explanation: diskonto esi des prosento.

steps.question: How do you ask 'how many liters of water do you need?'
options: komo litro di akwa tu neda?
kwanto tu neda litro di akwa?
kwanto litro di akwa tu neda?
steps.explanation: kwanto litro di akwa (how many liters of water) + tu neda (do you need).

lessons.title: The Bridge
lessons.subtitle: Furthermore, in fact, therefore — advanced connectors.

steps.title: The Bridge
steps.text: Foundation gave you e (and), o (or), pero (but), porke (because). Now you learn advanced connectors that build sophisticated arguments and flowing prose.

steps.sentence: ademas, mi sabe ke tu esi bona
steps.translation: furthermore, I know that you are good
in fact, you are the strongest

steps.question: How do you say 'in fact, this is not good'?
steps.explanation: enfakta (in fact) + iti no esi bona (this is not good).

steps.sentence: tu debe reposa, altramente tu esi lasa
steps.translation: you must rest, otherwise you will be tired

steps.sentence: mi esi hambre, dono mi kani
steps.translation: I am hungry, so I eat

steps.title: Building arguments
steps.text: Advanced connectors let you build complex arguments, give examples, make concessions, and draw conclusions — all essential for fluent conversation.
steps.auma: mi ama natura. ademas, natura dona sanita. sinembargo, we debe respeta natura. porekzemplo, we devri respeta arbo. konklusio, we debe respeta natura.
steps.english: I love nature. Furthermore, nature gives health. However, we must respect nature. For example, we should not cut trees. In conclusion, we should respect nature.

steps.question: How do you say 'I read while the child plays'?
steps.explanation: mi legi dum sina juga (I read while the child plays).

steps.question: How do you say 'you must practice, otherwise you will not know'?
options: altramente tu no sabe tu debe pratika
tu debe pratika, altramente tu no sabe
tu debe pratika altramente tu no sabe
steps.explanation: tu debe pratika (you must practice) + altramente (otherwise) + tu no sabe (you will not know).

steps.translation: We talk it through together in conflict.

lessons.title: The Source
lessons.subtitle: Evidentiality markers — how you know what you know.

steps.title: The Source
steps.text: Auma has a unique feature: evidentiality markers. These small words tell the listener how you know what you are saying — by direct experience, by hearing, by intuition, or by reasoning. This is rare in most languages but natural in Auma.

steps.translation: I sense (intuitively) that they are good
I heard that the island is beautiful

steps.sentence: padi, tu esi lasa porke tu kuri molta
steps.translation: I deduce that you are tired because you run a lot
I see that the sky is blue

steps.title: The four ways of knowing
steps.text: nuna = I see it (direct). odi = I heard it (hearsay). intu = I feel it (intuition). padi = I deduce it (reasoning). Place these at the start of a sentence to mark your source of knowledge.
steps.auma: nuna, pluva esi en sielo · odi, merkato teni diskonto · intu, ami di mi esi trisa · padi, tu no domi bona
steps.english: I see: rain is in the sky · I hear: the market has a discount · I sense: my friend is sad · I deduce: you did not sleep well

steps.question: If you heard that there is a festival tomorrow, how do you say it?
steps.explanation: odi for hearsay: odi, festa esi doma.

steps.translation: I am still reading the book

steps.title: Temporal attitude markers
steps.text: yari (ready/willing), suda (already — you met it on Day 9), ankora (still/yet), and pasa (past marker: was/did) add temporal nuance. They tell the listener about timing and readiness without changing the verb.
steps.auma: mi suda trova isla · mi ankora serka · mi pasa esi en boski · mi esi yari a rekina
steps.english: I already found the island · I am still searching · I was in the forest · I am ready to restart

steps.question: How do you say 'I already know the answer'?
steps.explanation: mi suda sabe (I already know) + responda (the answer).

steps.question: How do you say 'I deduce that you are still tired'?
steps.explanation: padi (I deduce) + tu ankora esi lasa (you are still tired).

lessons.title: The Nuance
lessons.subtitle: Weak, different, complex, connected — advanced qualities.

steps.title: The Nuance
steps.text: Your quality vocabulary expands with words for weakness, difference, complexity, connection, urgency, lostness, heaviness, and lightness. These add precision to every description.

steps.question: How do you say 'we are all different but connected'?
steps.explanation: we esi difa pero konekta (we are different but connected).

steps.translation: I feel lost in the city

steps.title: Nuanced descriptions
steps.text: With these words you can describe contrast, urgency, connection, and physical properties. Combine them with comparisons and discourse markers.
steps.auma: monta esi pesada e petra esi pesada, pero maripi esi levi · mi senti perdita sinembargo mi sabe ke mi esi konekta a komunita di mi · iti esi urjenta e kompla
steps.english: the mountain is heavy and rock is heavy, but the butterfly is light · I feel lost however I know that I am connected to my community · this is urgent and complex

steps.question: How do you say 'the message is urgent, you must read it now'?
options: mesaja esi urjenta, tu debe legi ita nau
mesaja urjenta esi, tu legi debe ita nau
urjenta esi mesaja, nau tu debe legi ita
steps.explanation: mesaja esi urjenta (the message is urgent) + tu debe legi ita nau (you must read it now).

steps.question: How do you say 'I feel weak but I am not lost'?
options: mi senti debio mi no esi perdita pero
mi senti debio pero mi no esi perdita
debio mi senti pero perdita mi no esi
steps.explanation: mi senti debio (I feel weak) + pero mi no esi perdita (but I am not lost).

lessons.title: The Expansion
lessons.subtitle: Expansion graduation — broad conversational mastery in Auma.

steps.title: The Expansion
steps.text: Fifty-six days. Nearly five hundred words. You began Foundation by saying mi esi bona. Now you can ask who, what, where, when, why, and how. You can express ability, obligation, and possibility. You can compare, intensify, and negate with precision. You can talk about time, seasons, health, nature, food, technology, business, art, philosophy, and consciousness itself. You have evidentiality markers and advanced connectors. You have the nuanced vocabulary of a real speaker. The expansion is complete. The depth is in you.

steps.title: Extended reading
steps.text: Read this passage aloud. It uses vocabulary from all eight weeks of Foundation and Expansion.
steps.auma: salama, ami. komo tu senti hodi? mi suda skrivi iti en auma porke mi kreda ke auma esi lingwa di kira. enfakta, tota vorto en auma teni signifa. porekzemplo, auma signifa au (spirito) e ma (unita) — spirito en unita, kira konekta. mi pratika auma en han-des-sisa dina. mi sabe kwanto vorto e mi pude konstrui frasa kompla. mi pratika tota dina e mi senti plu inspira. sinembargo, mi sabe ke konosia neva suda — mi debe sempre pratika plu. sabina beni de tempo e pratika. enton, kosa mi sabe nau? mi sabe ke bonina esi en tota vita. mi sabe ke belina esi en natura — en korali di mara, en maripi di boski, en loto di mara. mi sabe ke ubuntu esi bona: mi esi porke we esi. iti esi signifa di auma. konklusio, mi dona gratao a tu, ami — por parla, por rongo, por pratika kon mi. ademas, mi dona promisa: mi sempre pratika. sorao esi en kora di mi. mi esi yari a rekina. tu esi kori e sabina. we esi konekta. adio, ami. salama.
steps.english: Hello, friend. How do you feel today? I have already written this in Auma because I believe that Auma is the language of consciousness. In fact, every word in Auma has meaning. For example, Auma means au (spirit) and ma (unity) — spirit in unity, consciousness connected. I have practiced Auma for fifty-six days. I know many words and I can build complex sentences. I practice every day and I feel more inspired. However, I know that knowledge is never complete — I must always practice more. Wisdom comes from time and practice. So, what do I know now? I know that goodness is in all life. I know that beauty is in nature — in the coral of the sea, in the butterfly of the forest, in the lotus of the sea. I know that ubuntu is good: I am because we are. This is the meaning of Auma. In conclusion, I give thanks to you, friend — for speaking, for listening, for practicing with me. Furthermore, I give a promise: I will always practice. Hope is in my heart. I am ready to restart. You are courageous and wise. We are connected. Goodbye, friend. Peace.

steps.title: Full conversation
steps.text: Practice this dialogue. It uses vocabulary from all eight weeks.
steps.auma:
A: salama! suda molta tempo! komo tu esi?
B: beno, mi esi mui bona, gratao! mi suda pratika auma tota semana.
A: serio? kosa tu pratika iti semana?
B: mi pratika vorto por sanita e natura. porekzemplo, medika, balansa, korali, isla.
A: bona! mi rongo ke tu skrivi poema en auma. ka iti esi bona?
B: ya! enfakta, mi skrivi poema por mama di mi. iti esi sirka belina di verino.
A: mui inspira! ka tu pude legi ita a mi?
B: klaro! intu, iti esi bona poema: belina di verino esi en tota flora. sabina di tana esi en tota vorto. sorao di yuna esi en tota sonia. konklusio, vita esi bona.
A: iti esi mui bona arto. mi senti kori kwando mi rongo ita. ademas, mi kreda ke tu suda teni sabina.
B: gratao, ami. sinembargo, mi ankora pratika. sabina neva suda.
A: ubuntu, ami. we pratika porke we esi konekta. adio!
steps.english:
A: Hello! It has been a long time! How are you?
B: Well, I am very good, thanks! I have been practicing Auma all week.
A: Seriously? What did you practice this week?
B: I practiced words for health and nature. For example, medicine, balance, coral, island.
A: Good! I hear that you write poems in Auma. Is it good?
B: Yes! In fact, I wrote a poem for my mother. It is about the beauty of spring.
A: Very inspiring! Can you read it to me?
B: Of course! I sense it is a good poem: The beauty of spring is in every flower. The wisdom of the elder is in every word. The hope of the young is in every dream. In conclusion, life is good.
A: That is very good art. I feel courageous when I hear it. Furthermore, I believe that you already have wisdom.
B: Thank you, friend. However, I still practice. Wisdom is never complete.
A: Ubuntu, friend. We practice because we are connected. Goodbye!

steps.title: Expansion Graduation
steps.text: You have completed the Auma Expansion. Eight weeks. Over two hundred new words built on the Foundation. You can now hold real conversations, express complex ideas, argue with evidence, and describe the world with nuance. The language is no longer something you study — it is something you speak. The mastery tier awaits.
steps.auma: gratao, ami. tu esi plu ke pronta — tu esi yari. kira di tu esi klaro. konosia di tu esi granda. kora di tu esi konekta a komunita di we. we senti ubuntu. salama.
steps.english: Thank you, friend. You are more than ready — you are willing. Your consciousness is clear. Your knowledge is great. Your heart is connected to our community. We feel ubuntu. Peace.

lessons.title: The Beloved
lessons.subtitle: Partners, lovers, widows, exes — the full circle of romantic bonds.

steps.title: The Beloved
steps.text: You already know mama, papa, sina, sibra, ami, and marito. Today you complete the relationship vocabulary — partners, lovers, exes, and the bonds of the heart. Auma also has three derived forms of ama (love) that express different dimensions of connection.

steps.title: The life of bonds
steps.text: Relationships change over time. Auma gives you words for the full arc — from partner to spouse to widow to ex.

steps.meaning: children / child group (regular plural of sina + -li)

steps.title: The three faces of love
steps.text: Auma derives three forms from ama (love): amala is unconditional love, amara is romantic love, amana is communal love. The suffix changes the type of love expressed.
steps.auma: amala · amara · amana
steps.english: unconditional love · romantic love · communal love

steps.translation: mother feels unconditional love for children
I feel romantic love for you

steps.question: How do you say 'my beloved is calm'?
steps.explanation: alohi di mi (my beloved) + esi (is) + kalma (calm).

steps.question: Which word means 'romantic love'?
steps.explanation: amara is romantic love, amala is unconditional, amana is communal.

steps.question: How do you say 'the widow is strong'?
steps.explanation: Subject (viduo) + verb (esi) + descriptor (forta).

steps.question: How do you say 'our children are happy'?
steps.explanation: sinali di we (our children, inclusive) + esi hapi (are happy).

lessons.title: The Modifier
lessons.subtitle: Only, finally, still, both — the small words that change everything.

steps.title: The Modifier
steps.text: Today you learn the small words that change meaning dramatically. Modifiers, conjunctions, and particles — these are the glue of fluent speech. Each one reshapes how a sentence feels.

steps.title: Direction of time
steps.text: abi and ven mark direction in time. abi points to a habitual or ongoing action, ven points to something about to happen.
steps.auma: mi abi kani → mi ven kani
steps.english: I have been eating → I am about to eat

steps.title: Passive voice with -iva
steps.text: To say something was done to something without naming who did it, add the passive suffix -iva after a hyphen. The root never changes: kani becomes kani-iva, skrivi becomes skrivi-iva, koka becomes koka-iva, and lava becomes lava-iva. The pattern is: object + esi + verb-root-iva. The hyphen keeps the suffix visually separate from ita = that.
steps.auma: pano esi kani-iva · libro esi skrivi-iva · sopa esi koka-iva · tomo esi lava-iva
steps.english: the bread is eaten · the book is written · the soup is cooked · the house is cleaned

steps.sentence: libro esi dona-iva a mi par ami
steps.translation: the book is given to me by a friend

steps.title: The AUMA tense system
steps.text: AUMA marks time with particles placed BEFORE the verb. You now know te (just happened) and ven (about to happen). The full system has four markers: te (just), ven (about to), pasa (past — taught Day 74), and fura (future — taught Day 81). Without any particle, AUMA sentences are present tense by default. With context words like yesta or doma, the time is clear. The particles add precision: mi pasa kani = I ate. mi fura kani = I will eat.

steps.title: Connecting ideas
steps.text: You already know e (and), o (or), pero (but), and de (from/of). Now add asta (until), tala (such/so that), and koma (like/as).

steps.question: How do you say 'I only want water'?
steps.explanation: solo (only) modifies the subject: mi solo voli akwa.

steps.question: Which word means 'about to / going to'?
steps.explanation: ven points forward in time — about to happen.

steps.question: How do you say 'you are like a star'?
steps.explanation: koma (like/as) connects the comparison: tu esi koma stela.

steps.question: How do you say 'I will practice until evening'?
steps.explanation: mi ven pratika (I will practice) + asta sera (until evening).

lessons.title: The Harvest
lessons.subtitle: Cocoa, noodles, nuts, papaya — the global pantry in Auma.

steps.title: The Harvest
steps.text: You already know akwa, pano, keso, salo, dulsa, kopi, teo, and sopa. Today you fill out the pantry with fruits, grains, and staples from around the world.

steps.title: The global kitchen
steps.text: Auma borrows food words transparently from world languages. You can already guess many of them.

steps.sentence: pesao kon risao esi manja di sera

steps.question: How do you say 'I want to drink cocoa'?
steps.explanation: mi voli (I want) + beva (to drink) + kokoa (cocoa).

steps.question: How do you say 'rice with vegetables is good'?
steps.explanation: risao kon legu (rice with vegetables) + esi bona (is good).

steps.question: Which word means 'fish (food)'?
steps.explanation: pesao is fish as food; pesa is the living fish.

steps.question: How do you say 'mango is my fruit'?
steps.explanation: mango esi (mango is) + frutao di mi (my fruit).

lessons.title: The Temple
lessons.subtitle: Teeth, tongue, spine, shoulder — naming the body in full.

steps.title: The Temple
steps.text: You already know korpo, kapo, oki, boka, mano, kora. Today you name the body in full — from hair to toes. Your body is a temple. Name every part of it.

steps.title: Inside the mouth
steps.text: The mouth (boka) contains the tongue (linga), the teeth (denti), and the stomach (stoma) processes what enters.

steps.sentence: linga esi por parla e kani
steps.translation: the tongue is for speaking and eating

steps.title: Hands and feet
steps.text: You know mano (hand). Now learn dita (finger), gamba (leg), and peda (foot) — the limbs that move you through the world.

steps.sentence: mi teni des dita en mano
steps.translation: I have ten fingers on my hands

steps.question: How do you say 'my hair is good'?
steps.explanation: peli di mi (my hair) + esi bona (is good).

steps.question: Which word means 'shoulder'?
steps.explanation: spala is shoulder, stoma is stomach, dorso is back.

steps.question: How do you say 'my back feels pain'?
steps.explanation: dorso di mi (my back) + senti (feels) + dolo (pain).

steps.question: How do you say 'the tongue is for speaking and eating'?
options: linga esi por parla e kani
por parla e kani linga esi
linga por parla esi e kani
steps.explanation: linga esi (the tongue is) + por parla e kani (for speaking and eating).

lessons.title: The Sacred Place
lessons.subtitle: Temples, shrines, villages, fields — where life happens.

steps.title: The Sacred Place
steps.text: You know tomo (house), parko, kafe, merkato, ofisa, templo. Today you learn places sacred and domestic — shrines, villages, beaches, and rooms inside the home.

steps.translation: the shrine is on the mountain
the field is green and big
I want to go to the beach

steps.title: Settlement and community
steps.text: From the smallest village to the largest city — Auma names where people gather.

steps.sentence: vila di mi esi pika pero bona
steps.translation: my village is small but good

steps.sentence: pola esi inter vila e sita
steps.translation: a town is between a village and a city

steps.title: Rooms of the home
steps.text: Every home has rooms. Learn the spaces inside your tomo (house).

steps.translation: the roof of the house is red

steps.question: How do you say 'the children go to school'?
steps.explanation: sinali (children) + anda a (go to) + lerotano (school).

steps.question: Which word means 'shrine / sanctuary'?
steps.explanation: sanatano is a shrine/sanctuary, lerotano is a school, templo is a temple.

steps.question: How do you say 'I cook in the kitchen'?
steps.explanation: mi koka (I cook) + en kosina (in the kitchen).

steps.question: How do you say 'the field is green and big'?
steps.explanation: kampo esi (the field is) + verda e granda (green and big).

lessons.title: The Cry
lessons.subtitle: Wow, oops, shhh, hey — sounds that bypass grammar.

steps.title: The Cry
steps.text: Every language has sounds that bypass grammar — exclamations of surprise, pain, joy, and warning. Today you learn the interjections of Auma, plus three discourse words that anchor what you say in honesty.

steps.sentence: opa! libro di mi no esi en tomo
steps.translation: oops! my book is not at home

steps.title: Quick sounds
steps.text: Some interjections are just a breath — he for calling attention, uf for frustration, hm for thinking, sh for silence.

steps.title: Discourse anchors
steps.text: Three words that frame your speech with authenticity — basika (basically), enverda (truly), honesta (honestly).

steps.translation: basically, I want to practice more
truly, you are a good friend
honestly, I do not know the answer

steps.question: Which interjection means 'ouch / pain'?
steps.explanation: aya expresses pain, opa is oops, uf is frustration.

steps.question: How do you say 'shh! the baby is sleeping'?
steps.explanation: sh! (quiet) + nuri esi domi (the baby is sleeping).

steps.question: Which word means 'truly / in truth'?
steps.explanation: enverda means truly/in truth, honesta means honestly, basika means basically.

steps.question: How do you say 'hey! listen to me'?
steps.explanation: he! (hey) + rongo a mi (listen to me).

lessons.title: The Reflection
lessons.subtitle: Week 9 review — relationships, modifiers, food, body, places, and voice.

steps.title: The Reflection
steps.text: Week 9 gave you the full relationship vocabulary, modifiers that reshape meaning, the complete pantry, the entire body, sacred and domestic places, and the sounds of spontaneous expression. You have deepened from grammar into life.

steps.title: Reading passage
steps.text: Read this passage aloud. It uses vocabulary from Week 9 and all previous tiers.
steps.auma: salama, alohi. hodi mi ven parla de vita di we. novio di mi e mi esi en vila pika. we teni gardi kon flora e arbo. matina, mi koka en kosina — risao kon legu e buta. sinali kani banana e mango. tali esi hapi. sera, we esi en sala e parla. mi senti amala por sinali di we. honesta, vita en kampo esi koma sonia. dorso di mi senti dolo de pratika pero kora di mi esi bona. fin, mi sabe ke amana esi plu granda ke tomo — iti esi komunita.
steps.english: Hello, beloved. Today I will speak about our life. My partner and I are in a small village. We have a garden with flowers and trees. In the morning, I cook in the kitchen — rice with vegetables and butter. The children eat banana and mango. They are happy. In the evening, we sit in the living room and talk. I feel unconditional love for our children. Honestly, life in the countryside is like a dream. My back feels pain from work but my heart is good. Finally, I know that communal love is bigger than a house — it is community.

steps.question: What does 'amala' mean?
steps.explanation: amala is unconditional love, amara is romantic, amana is communal.

steps.question: How do you say 'I am about to sleep'?
steps.explanation: ven marks something about to happen: mi ven domi.

steps.question: Which word means 'kitchen'?
steps.explanation: kosina is kitchen, sala is living room, bano is bathroom.

steps.question: How do you say 'my nose is small'?
steps.explanation: naso di mi (my nose) + esi pika (is small).

steps.question: Which interjection expresses surprise/amazement?
steps.explanation: wa means wow/amazing, uf is frustration, hm is thinking.

steps.question: How do you say 'both friends are good'?
steps.explanation: ambi (both) + ami (friends) + esi bona (are good).

steps.question: What does 'basika' mean?
steps.explanation: basika means basically, honesta means honestly, enverda means truly.

lessons.title: The Craft I
lessons.subtitle: Film, photograph, win, guide — verbs of skill and creation.

steps.title: The Craft I
steps.text: You already know many verbs — anda, kuri, nada, salta, flugi, lava, koka. Today begins a three-day verb intensive. These are verbs of skill, creation, and consequence.

steps.translation: you photograph flowers in the garden
the elder guides the children to school

steps.title: Verbs of action and change
steps.text: kesi means to stop or cease. kina means to move or stir. kona means to know through experience. lero means to learn.

steps.sentence: mi kona dolo e mi kona hapi
steps.translation: I know pain and I know happiness
put the book on the bed

steps.question: How do you say 'I film our celebration'?
steps.explanation: mi filma (I film) + festa di we (our celebration).

steps.question: Which word means 'stop / cease'?
steps.explanation: kesi is stop, kina is move, kona is know by experience.

steps.question: How do you say 'put the book on the bed'?
steps.explanation: pona (put) + libro (book) + en kama (on the bed).

steps.question: How do you say 'they win the game'?
steps.explanation: ta (they) + gana (win) + juga (game).

lessons.title: The Craft II
lessons.subtitle: Cry, massage, mix, be born — verbs of becoming and transformation.

steps.title: The Craft II
steps.text: Today you learn verbs of becoming and transformation — crying, mixing, being born, leaving, and the deepest actions of consciousness.

steps.sentence: nuri laka porke ta esi hambre
steps.translation: the baby cries because they are hungry
the baby is born in the morning

steps.title: Going and being
steps.text: parti means to leave or depart. pali means to say or tell — parla (Day 7) is the activity of speaking; pali reports the words themselves. mori is to die. medita is to meditate — the verb of inner stillness.

steps.question: How do you say 'the baby cries because they are hungry'?
options: laka nuri porke hambre ta esi
nuri laka porke ta esi hambre
steps.explanation: nuri laka (baby cries) + porke (because) + ta esi hambre (they are hungry).

steps.question: Which word means 'be born'?
steps.explanation: nasi is be born, mori is die, parti is leave.

steps.question: How do you say 'mix fruit with milk'?
steps.explanation: miksa (mix) + frutao (fruit) + kon lakto (with milk).

steps.question: How do you say 'I meditate every morning'?
steps.explanation: mi medita (I meditate) + tota matina (every morning).

lessons.title: The Craft III
lessons.subtitle: Sit, cut, separate, suck — verbs of precision and action.

steps.title: The Craft III
steps.text: The final verb batch — precise actions: sitting, cutting, separating, uniting. These complete your active vocabulary.

steps.translation: sit in the living room and rest
I cut bread with my hand

steps.title: Time, sound, and union
steps.text: timi means to time or measure duration. sora means to sound or ring. uni means to unite or join. vesti means to dress or wear.

steps.question: How do you say 'I separate good from bad'?
steps.explanation: mi separi (I separate) + bona de malu (good from bad).

steps.question: Which word means 'unite / join'?
steps.explanation: uni is unite, separi is separate, miksa is mix.

steps.question: How do you say 'music sounds in the temple'?
steps.explanation: musika sora (music sounds) + en templo (in the temple).

steps.question: How do you say 'sit in the living room and rest'?
steps.explanation: seda (sit) + en sala (in the living room) + e reposa (and rest).

lessons.title: The Network
lessons.subtitle: Apps, data, batteries, WiFi — the deeper digital vocabulary.

steps.title: The Network
steps.text: You know komputa, telefona, reta, skirmo, tekla, klika, senda, resiva, karga, konto. Today you go deeper into digital life — apps, data, social media, and the infrastructure of connection.

steps.translation: the phone battery is small / low

steps.title: Media and access
steps.text: video, foto, wifai, kargador — the tools of modern communication.

steps.translation: I film a video for social media
I need a charger for my phone
I send a link to you
I do not want social media today
I upload a photo to the network

steps.question: How do you say 'the phone battery is small / low'?
steps.explanation: bateria di telefona (phone battery) + esi pika (is small / low). The more precise word basa is taught later.

steps.question: Which word means 'download / upload'?
steps.explanation: subi is download/upload, senda is send, karga is charge/load.

steps.question: How do you say 'I send a link to you'?
steps.explanation: mi senda (I send) + linka (a link) + a tu (to you).

steps.question: How do you say 'is the WiFi good here?'?
steps.explanation: ka (question) + wifai esi bona (WiFi is good) + hiro (here).

lessons.title: The Bestiary
lessons.subtitle: Dolphins, cats, dogs, insects — the creatures of Auma.

steps.title: The Bestiary
steps.text: You know anima, avi, pesa, maripi. Today you meet the creatures and habitats of Auma — dolphins, cats, dogs, snakes, and the nests and lakes they call home.

steps.translation: the dolphin swims in the sea

steps.sentence: feli domi en kama di mi
steps.translation: the cat sleeps on my bed

steps.title: Reptiles and birds
steps.text: tortu is turtle, serpa is snake, rana is frog, korvo is crow. These creatures complete the Auma bestiary.

steps.translation: the turtle is slow but wise
the snake is in the grass
the frog jumps in the lake
the crow is black and good

steps.title: Habitats and growth
steps.text: Every creature needs a home. nido is nest, koli is hill, fola is leaf, herba is grass, wata is water (as element), lako is lake.

steps.translation: the bird builds a nest in the tree
the leaf of the tree is green
the grass is green in the field
the water of the lake is clear
the lake is serene in the morning

steps.question: How do you say 'the dolphin swims in the sea'?
steps.explanation: delfina nada (the dolphin swims) + en mara (in the sea).

steps.question: Which word means 'nest'?
steps.explanation: nido is nest, koli is hill, fola is leaf.

steps.question: How do you say 'the frog jumps in the lake'?
steps.explanation: rana salta (the frog jumps) + en lako (in the lake).

steps.question: How do you say 'the cat sleeps on my bed'?
options: feli en kama domi di mi
domi feli en kama di mi
feli domi en kama di mi
steps.explanation: feli domi (the cat sleeps) + en kama di mi (on my bed).

lessons.title: The Measure
lessons.subtitle: Tall, short, wide, narrow — physical dimensions and scale.

steps.title: The Measure
steps.text: You know bona, malu, nova, varma, frida. Today you learn the physical dimensions — tall and short, wide and narrow, big and small. These are the qualities of space and scale.

steps.title: Size review
steps.text: You learned granda (big) and pika (small) in Week 1. Now we use them with precise measurement: alta (tall), basa (short/low), kurta (short length), larga (wide).

steps.title: Length and width
steps.text: longa is long, kurta is short (length). larga is wide, streta is narrow. These describe objects, paths, and spaces.

steps.translation: the road is narrow in the village

steps.title: Age, speed, and strength
steps.text: anti is old (opposite of nova). veka is ancient/elderly. rapi is fast/quick. fortao is strong (as quality noun).

steps.translation: the tree is ancient and big
the dolphin is fast in the sea

steps.question: How do you say 'the mountain is tall'?
steps.explanation: monta esi (the mountain is) + alta (tall).

steps.question: Which pair are opposites?
steps.explanation: larga (wide) and streta (narrow) are opposites.

steps.question: How do you say 'the tree is ancient and big'?
steps.explanation: arbo esi (the tree is) + veka e granda (ancient and big).

steps.question: How do you say 'the road is narrow in the village'?
steps.explanation: via esi streta (the road is narrow) + en vila (in the village).

lessons.title: The Reflection
lessons.subtitle: Week 10 review — verbs, technology, nature, and dimensions.

steps.title: The Reflection
steps.text: Week 10 gave you twenty-four new verbs of skill and consequence, the full digital vocabulary, the creatures and habitats of Auma, and the dimensions of the physical world. You can now describe what you do, what you see, and the shape of everything around you.

steps.title: Reading passage
steps.text: Read this passage aloud. It uses vocabulary from Week 10 and all previous tiers.
steps.auma: hodi mi parti de sita granda e mi anda a lako. via esi longa e streta pero mi kina rapida. kwando mi beni a lako, mi nuna ke wata esi klaro e sereni. delfina nada en mara lonta pero hiro rana salta en herba. feli di mi seda en petra e rongo avi en arbo. mi fota tota — foto di fola verda, di korvo nera, di nido en arbo alta. mi subi foto a sosia pero pos mi bloka sosia porke mi voli reposa. mi seda en herba, mi rongo sora di wata, e mi medita. basika, natura esi plu bona ke reta.
steps.english: Today I leave the big city and I go to the lake. The road is long and narrow but I move quickly. When I come to the lake, I see that the water is clear and serene. Dolphins swim in the distant sea but here frogs jump in the grass. My cat sits on a rock and listens to birds in the tree. I photograph everything — photos of green leaves, of black crows, of nests in tall trees. I upload photos to social media but then I block social media because I want to rest. I sit in the grass, I listen to the sound of water, and I meditate. Basically, nature is better than the internet.

steps.question: Which word means 'photograph / take a photo'?
steps.explanation: fota is the verb (to photograph), filma is to film, foto is the noun (photo).

steps.question: How do you say 'I move my body'?
steps.explanation: mi kina (I move) + korpo di mi (my body).

steps.question: Which word means 'lake'?
steps.explanation: lako is lake, rivo is river, mara is sea.

steps.question: How do you say 'the bird builds a nest in the tree'?
steps.explanation: avi konstrui (the bird builds) + nido (a nest) + en arbo (in the tree).

steps.question: What does 'rapi' mean?
steps.explanation: rapi means fast/quick, lenta means slow.

steps.question: How do you say 'I need a charger for my phone'?
steps.explanation: mi neda (I need) + kargador (charger) + por telefona (for phone).

steps.question: How do you say 'we unite for harmony'?
steps.explanation: we uni (we unite) + por armoni (for harmony).

lessons.title: The Deep
lessons.subtitle: Love, change, mind, circle — the concepts behind consciousness.

steps.title: The Deep
steps.text: You have learned the body, the world, the creatures, and the verbs. Now you enter the abstract — the concepts behind consciousness itself. Today: condition, change, mind, doubt, growth, death, birth, and three untranslatable concepts from world philosophy.

steps.translation: change is the nature of life

steps.sentence: mente di mi esi klaro hodi

steps.title: Life and death
steps.text: nasita is birth, morta is death, kresao is growth. These name the arc of all existence. dubio is doubt — the beginning of wisdom.

steps.sentence: dubio esi en mente di mi

steps.translation: the birth of a baby is a celebration
death is part of the circle

steps.title: The untranslatable
steps.text: sirkulo is the circle — the shape of all cycles. ikigai is borrowed from Japanese philosophy — it names the intersection of what you love, what you're good at, what the world needs, and what sustains you. wabi comes from the Japanese aesthetic tradition wabi-sabi — it honors the beauty found in imperfection, incompleteness, and impermanence. These words are borrowed with respect, preserving their original nuance.

steps.sentence: vita esi sirkulo de nasita e morta
steps.translation: life is a circle of birth and death

steps.sentence: ikigai di mi esi lero e parla auma
steps.translation: my life purpose is to learn and speak Auma

steps.sentence: wabi esi en tota kosa anti
steps.translation: beauty of imperfection is in every old thing

steps.question: Which word means 'condition / circumstance'?
steps.explanation: kondisio means condition or circumstance.

steps.question: Which word means 'life purpose / reason for being'?
steps.explanation: ikigai is life purpose, wabi is beauty of imperfection, sirkulo is circle.

steps.question: How do you say 'change is the nature of life'?
steps.explanation: kambio esi (change is) + natura di vita (the nature of life).

steps.question: How do you say 'death is part of the circle'?
steps.explanation: morta esi (death is) + parti de sirkulo (part of the circle).

steps.translation: I feel attachment in the heart.
I feel abandonment in the heart.

lessons.title: The Spectrum
lessons.subtitle: Brave, bored, humble, confused — the full emotional palette.

steps.title: The Spectrum
steps.text: You know hapi, trisa, sereni, ira, kalma, sola, inspira, kreati, foka, distra, kontenta, frustra, amora, kori, sabar. Today you complete the emotional palette — bravery, boredom, humility, anxiety, despair, and more.

steps.sentence: ta esi brani en tota kosa

steps.translation: the elder is humble and wise

steps.title: Pride, doubt, and gratitude
steps.text: proda is proud, dubi is doubtful, grata is grateful. These three shape how we see ourselves and others.

steps.translation: mother is proud of the children

steps.sentence: mi esi dubi de deside di mi
steps.translation: I am doubtful of my decision

steps.sentence: ta senti vako pos morta di ami
steps.translation: they feel emptiness after a friend dies
the children are bored at school

steps.sentence: no esi despa — spera esi hiro
steps.translation: do not despair — hope is here

steps.sentence: mente di mi esi klara nau
mi esi konfu — mi no sabe kemo
steps.translation: I am confused — I do not know why

steps.question: Which word means 'humble'?
steps.explanation: humi is humble, brani is brave, proda is proud.

steps.question: How do you say 'I am grateful for life'?
steps.explanation: mi esi grata (I am grateful) + por vita (for life).

steps.question: Which word means 'anxious / nervous'?
steps.explanation: ansi is anxious, despa is desperate, konfu is confused.

steps.question: How do you say 'you are strong and brave'?
steps.explanation: tu esi (you are) + forta e brani (strong and brave).

steps.translation: I feel projection in the heart.

steps.meaning: mentally slip away / dissociate-like spacing out
steps.sentence: si tu forglisa, senti mano e korpo
steps.translation: If you slip away, feel hand and body.
I feel fury in the heart.
The body is over-guarded after danger.

lessons.title: The Texture
lessons.subtitle: Clean, soft, dark, hard — qualities you can feel.

steps.title: The Texture
steps.text: You know qualities of size, temperature, and weight. Today you learn textures and abstract qualities — clean and dark, soft and hard, simple and difficult, full and few.

steps.translation: the night is dark and calm

steps.title: Truth and ease
steps.text: vera is true/real, simpla is simple, fasila is easy, difisa is difficult. These describe the nature of ideas and tasks.

steps.title: Fullness and value
steps.text: belao is beauty (as quality), kara is dear/expensive, klarao is clarity, moda is wet, plena is full, poka is few/little.

steps.sentence: alohi esi plu kara ke dora
steps.translation: the beloved is more precious than gold
the grass is wet from rain

steps.question: How do you say 'the water is clean'?
steps.explanation: akwa esi (the water is) + limpa (clean).

steps.question: Which pair are opposites?
steps.explanation: fasila (easy) and difisa (difficult) are opposites.

steps.question: How do you say 'the beloved is more precious than gold'?
options: plu kara alohi esi ke dora
alohi plu kara esi ke dora
alohi esi plu kara ke dora
steps.explanation: alohi esi (the beloved is) + plu kara ke dora (more precious than gold).

steps.question: What does 'plena' mean?
steps.explanation: plena is full, poka is few, limpa is clean.

lessons.title: The Clock
lessons.subtitle: Brief, long, first, often — mastering temporal precision.

steps.title: The Clock
steps.text: You know tempo, hodi, doma, yesta, nau, sempre, neva. Today you master temporal precision — brief and long, first and final, often and rarely, and the particles that pin actions to exact moments.

steps.sentence: iti esi fina vorto di mi

steps.title: Frequency
steps.text: ofta is often, rara is rarely, vesa is sometimes. These tell how frequently something happens.

steps.translation: I often meditate in the morning

steps.title: Moment markers
steps.text: te (Day 58) covers "just now / just happened". pronto means soon. ankora (Day 54) means still/yet/again. nau is the one canon word for now — older texts sometimes show na, nu, or justa, but those are deprecated: use nau and te. sona means sleep or slumber.

steps.question: How do you say 'life is brief'?
steps.explanation: vita esi (life is) + breva (brief).

steps.question: Which word means 'often / frequently'?
steps.explanation: ofta is often, rara is rarely, vesa is sometimes.

steps.question: How do you say 'I am still learning Auma'?
steps.explanation: mi ankora lero (I still learn) + auma.

steps.question: Which word means 'first'?
steps.explanation: prima is first, fina is final, breva is brief.

lessons.title: The Village
lessons.subtitle: Truth, respect, culture, tradition — the vocabulary of community.

steps.title: The Village
steps.text: Today you learn the vocabulary of community and the remaining emotions. Truth, respect, culture, tradition — the words that bind society. Plus the final emotional shadings: evil, pain, risk, sacred, thirsty, alive, and weak.

steps.sentence: verita esi plu forta ke falsa
sorio di tu dona hapi a mi
steps.translation: your smile gives happiness to me

steps.title: Culture and cooperation
steps.text: paso is peace/step, kultura is culture, tradisa is tradition, gotong is mutual cooperation (from gotong-royong).

steps.translation: the first step is always difficult
mutual cooperation is the heart of the village

steps.title: The final emotions
steps.text: mala is evil/wicked, peno is sorrow/grief, riska is risky/daring, santa is sacred/holy, tirsta is thirsty, sura is angry (sustained), viva is alive/vibrant, debi is weak (emotionally).

steps.translation: they are not evil — they are confused

steps.sentence: mi esi tirsta — dona akwa plisa
steps.translation: I am thirsty — give water please

steps.sentence: ta esi sura pero mi esi kalma
steps.translation: they are furious but I am calm

steps.sentence: mi senti debi pero mi no esi perdita
steps.translation: I feel weak but I am not lost

steps.question: How do you say 'truth is stronger than falsehood'?
options: verita plu forta esi ke falsa
verita esi plu forta ke falsa
plu forta verita esi ke falsa
steps.explanation: verita esi (truth is) + plu forta ke falsa (stronger than falsehood).

steps.question: Which word means 'mutual cooperation'?
steps.explanation: gotong is mutual cooperation, tradisa is tradition, kultura is culture.

steps.question: How do you say 'I feel alive in nature'?
steps.explanation: mi senti (I feel) + viva (alive) + en natura (in nature).

steps.question: Which word means 'sacred / holy'?
steps.explanation: santa is sacred, mala is evil, sura is furious.

lessons.title: The Precision
lessons.subtitle: Error taxonomy — naming what went wrong and why.

steps.title: The Precision
steps.text: Auma has a unique error taxonomy — seven specific words for different types of errors. This is the language of debugging, correction, and precision. You also learn two evidentiality markers that complete the source system.

steps.sentence: mi teni erospeka — mi pensa iti esi difa
steps.translation: I had the wrong expectation — I thought it was different

steps.title: The Reflection
steps.text: Week 11 took you into the depths — love, change, mind, doubt, the full emotional palette, textures and qualities, temporal mastery, community vocabulary, and the error taxonomy. You can now express the most abstract ideas in Auma with precision.

steps.title: Reading passage
steps.text: Read this passage aloud. It uses vocabulary from Week 11 and all previous tiers.
steps.auma: mi senti viva hodi. nau mi seda en gardi e mi pensa de sirkulo di vita. prima, nasita — nuri laka e rongo e lero. pos, kresao — mi lero de dubio, de peno, de pasi. mi ofta senti konfu pero ankora mi lero. vesa mi senti debi pero mi sabe ke kambio dona fortao. mi te rongo musika de templo e mi senti klarao en mente. ikigai di mi esi klaro: mi voli lero, mi voli parla verita, mi voli uni kon komunita. tradisa di we esi santa. gotong esi kora di kultura di we. honesta, mi esi grata. vita esi breva pero plena. enverda, mi ama vita e mi ama tota vorto di auma.
steps.english: I feel alive today. Right now I sit in the garden and I think about the circle of life. First, birth — the baby cries and listens and learns. Then, growth — I learn from doubt, from grief, from passion. I often feel confused but still I learn. Sometimes I feel weak but I know that change gives strength. I just heard music from the temple and I feel clarity in my mind. My life purpose is clear: I want to learn, I want to speak truth, I want to unite with community. Our tradition is sacred. Mutual cooperation is the heart of our culture. Honestly, I am grateful. Life is brief but full. Truly, I love life and I love every word of Auma.

lessons.title: The Raw

steps.title: The Raw
steps.text: Every living language has words for frustration, disgust, taboo, and raw emotional pressure. Today you learn Auma's hard swear words — not nerfed, not childish — plus the mathematical operations that represent the precision end of the spectrum.

steps.title: Cultural note on swearing
steps.text: Auma treats hard profanity as emotional release and intensity, not as hate. You may say fuck, shit, damn, or call out cruel behavior, but Auma does not canonize identity slurs, dehumanizing attacks, or punching down. The rule is simple: pressure-release is allowed; hate is not.
