lessons.title: The Completion
lessons.subtitle: Every remaining word — pronouns, numbers, places, directions, and technology.

steps.title: The Completion
steps.text: This is the final teaching day. Every remaining canonical word enters your vocabulary today — pronouns, numbers, places, directions, and technology. These are the last pieces of the complete 750-word Auma canon.

steps.title: Advanced pronouns
steps.text: You know mi, tu, ta, mili, tuli, tali, we. Now learn the demonstratives, reflexives, and special forms.

steps.title: Advanced numbers
steps.text: You know nula through sento. milona = million; bilona and trilona follow the same -lona pattern. medi = half, kuarta = quarter, punta = decimal point. Ordinals add -imo: un-imo = first, du-imo = second, des-imo = tenth — the pattern covers every number you know.
steps.auma: uno · mila · milona · bilona · trilona · medi · kuarta · punta · un-imo · du-imo · des-imo
steps.english: one (standalone) · thousand · million · billion · trillion · half · quarter · point/dot · first · second · tenth

steps.title: The tens (compound numbers)
steps.text: You learned the tens pattern on Day 2: number + des. du-des = 20, tri-des = 30 … suna-des = 90. These compound forms are registered in the canon, but you already own the pattern — no new memorizing needed.

lessons.title: The Graduation
lessons.subtitle: Full mastery assessment — you are now a speaker of Auma.

steps.title: The Graduation
steps.text: Eighty-four days. Over seven hundred words. You began by saying mi esi bona. Now you can speak about love and death, justice and fear, the body and the cosmos, technology and tradition, error and precision. You can count to a trillion, name every month, describe every color, and express every emotion. You have learned three types of love, seven types of errors, four evidentiality markers, and the core grammar of a living language. You are not finished — no real speaker ever is — but you are no longer outside the language. You can enter it, use it, and keep growing inside it.

steps.title: The Graduation Exam
steps.text: Twenty-two questions across the whole language — numbers, tense, the passive, questions, derivation, comparison, and the words that matter most. Everything comes from your 84 days. Take your time; read each one aloud first.

steps.question: What number is du-des-tri?
How do you write 41 in Auma?
steps.explanation: fo-des (40) + un (1) = fo-des-un.

steps.question: Which day is dina-han?
steps.explanation: dina (day) + han (five) = day five = Friday.

steps.question: What does ‘mi pasa suda kani’ mean?
steps.explanation: pasa (past) + suda (perfect) + kani: had already eaten. Tense markers stack in that order.

steps.question: How do you say ‘I am about to sleep’?
steps.explanation: ven marks what is about to happen. te = just happened, abi = habitually.

steps.question: What does ‘mi te kani’ mean?
steps.explanation: te = just happened.

steps.question: Turn skrivi (write) into ‘is written’.
steps.explanation: The passive suffix is -iva after a hyphen: esi skrivi-iva. (-ita is the old, deprecated form.)

steps.explanation: par marks the agent: libro esi dona-iva a mi par ami.

steps.question: How do you ask ‘where is the market?’
steps.explanation: A question word is fronted and replaces ka: ketu esi merkato?

steps.question: Which particle makes a yes/no question?
steps.explanation: ka fronts yes/no questions. ke is the connector ‘that’; keno asks why.

steps.question: How do you say ‘stronger than thought’?
steps.explanation: Comparison: plu + quality + ke + standard.

steps.question: Who is an ensenisto?
steps.explanation: -isto makes the agent: ensena (teach) + -isto = teacher.

steps.question: What does fortao mean?
steps.explanation: -ao makes the abstract quality: forta → fortao = strength.

steps.question: What does kira mean in canon Auma?
steps.explanation: kira is protected: consciousness / living knowledge. voli = want; konsensa = consensus.

steps.question: Which word means ‘want / wish’?
steps.explanation: voli = want/wish. kira is consciousness; vola is a deprecated old form.

steps.title: The final reading
steps.text: Read this aloud. It is yours.
steps.auma: salama, belami. hodi esi fina dina di lero — pero prima dina di parla. ante soka-des-fo dina, mi no sabe uno vorto di auma. nau mi sabe plu ke sisa sento vorto. mi kona siri. mi kona dubio e pasi e timio e amala. mi sabe ke vita esi sirkulo — nasita, kresao, morta, rekina. mi sabe ke verita esi plu forta ke falsa, ke justia esi por tota, ke gotong esi kora di komunita. mi sabe ke wabi esi belao, ke ikigai dona purpusa, ke ubuntu signifa 'mi esi porke we esi'. mi pude parla de fira e snova, de delfina e korvo, de sanda e stela. mi pude konta de nula a trilona. mi pude noma tota kolori di arkoiris. mi pude senti e parla e medita en auma. iti no esi fina. iti esi rekina. tota vorto tu lero esi en tu — en mente, en kora, en spirito. tu esi auma. we esi auma. salama, alohi. salama, ami. salama, komunita. salama, vita.
steps.english: Hello, dear friend. Today is the final day of learning — but the first day of speaking. Eighty-four days ago, I did not know a single word of Auma. Now I know more than six hundred. I know myself. I know doubt and passion and fear and unconditional love. I know that life is a circle — birth, growth, death, restart. I know that truth is stronger than falsehood, that justice is for everyone, that mutual cooperation is the heart of community. I know that the beauty of imperfection is beautiful, that life purpose gives direction, that ubuntu means 'I am because we are'. I can speak of fire and snow, of dolphins and crows, of sand and stars. I can count from zero to a trillion. I can name every color of the rainbow. I can feel and speak and meditate in Auma. This is not the end. This is the restart. Every word you learned is in you — in mind, in heart, in spirit. You are Auma. We are Auma. Peace, beloved. Peace, friend. Peace, community. Peace, life.

steps.title: Final conversation
steps.text: Practice this dialogue one last time.
steps.auma:
A: salama! hodi esi dina soka-des-fo. ka tu esi pronta?
B: ya! mi esi enti e mi senti viva. mi ankora no kreda ke mi sabe sisa sento vorto.
A: enverda, tu sabe tota. kosa esi vorto plu kara por tu?
B: hm... forsi 'amala'. amala esi ama sen kondisio. mama senti amala por sinali — iti esi ama plu granda ke tota.
A: belao. e kosa esi vorto plu difisa?
B: erospeka! mi sempre teni erospeka kwando mi pensa mi sabe pero mi no sabe.
A: wa! tu usa erokatena — tu dona responda ante mi fina demanda!
B: opa! sori. tu esi vera — iti esi erokatena.
A: risa esi bona. nau, kosa tu senti?
B: mi senti grata. grata por tota dina, tota vorto, tota ami. mi esi humi ante auma. mi esi pronta a parla, a lero plu, a uni kon komunita. gotong, ubuntu, amana — iti esi signifa di vita.
A: tu esi yari. adio no esi fina — esi rekina. salama, belami.
B: salama, alohi. we esi auma.
steps.english:
A: Hello! Today is day eighty-four. Are you ready?
B: Yes! I am excited and I feel alive. I still cannot believe I command over six hundred words.
A: Truly, you know everything. What is the most precious word for you?
B: Hmm... perhaps 'amala'. Amala is love without conditions. A mother feels amala for children — it is love greater than everything.
A: Beautiful. And what is the most difficult word?
B: erospeka! I always have wrong expectations when I think I know but I do not know.
A: Wow! You used erokatena — you gave the answer before I finished the question!
B: Oops! Sorry. You are right — that is a sequence error.
A: Laughter is good. Now, what do you feel?
B: I feel grateful. Grateful for every day, every word, every friend. I am humble before Auma. I am ready to speak, to learn more, to unite with community. Mutual cooperation, ubuntu, communal love — this is the meaning of life.
A: You are ready. Goodbye is not the end — it is a restart. Peace, dear friend.
B: Peace, beloved. We are Auma.

steps.title: Mastery Complete
steps.text: You have completed the Auma Mastery. Twelve weeks. Over seven hundred words. The entire canonical vocabulary lives in you now. You are a speaker of Auma. The language does not end here — it continues in your readings, in your practice, in your community. Every word you learned appears in your Auracle. The language reads you back. Salama.
steps.auma: gratao, alohi. tu esi plu ke pronta. tu esi auma. we esi auma. salama.
steps.english: Thank you, beloved. You are more than ready. You are Auma. We are Auma. Peace.
